project-roadmap.title: Build a learning-profile page for a student-success team
project-roadmap.bodyMarkdown:
You are a **junior web developer** helping a student-success team prepare a small learning-profile page for a new-coder orientation. The team needs one clean file—`index.html`—that they can open in a browser and review without any extra setup. Your deliverable is a browser-ready page that clearly shows what the learner is studying and demonstrates sound HTML structure.

You will build that deliverable in three progressive steps. First, create the document foundation in `index.html`. Next, add the visible heading and paragraph content the team asked for. Finally, improve the page structure with a second heading and nested emphasis while keeping the document valid. Each step continues the same file, so preserve the working markup from the previous milestone rather than starting over.

Use the browser preview after every change as if you were checking the page before handing it to the team. The preview should remain understandable throughout the project: first the document has a reliable foundation, then the reviewer sees useful content, and finally the page gains clearer structure and emphasis. **Check Answer** verifies the required HTML source for each milestone.

The goal is not decoration. The finished `index.html` is the team's review copy and should demonstrate that you can organize a modern HTML document, separate head information from body content, use headings and paragraphs, keep tags balanced, and nest elements correctly. Later CSS and JavaScript courses can build on this same web-development workflow.
